title: Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.
notes: Marvel Television (division, 2010–2019). Not part of Wikipedia's MCU timeline diagram or the Disney+ timeline; canon status is ambiguous, so tier is 'adjacent'. Placements come from Wikipedia tie-in statements and MCU Fandom wiki year pages (see each season's note).

in_universe.note: Wikipedia (season 1): "the episode "The Well" takes place directly after the events of Thor: The Dark World (2013)", with a Winter Soldier tie-in; article categories "Television series set in 2013/2014". MCU Fandom wiki (2013): an ID badge reads "2013SEP09", placing the opening episodes in September 2013.

Wikipedia (season 2): Clark Gregg "stated that the season resumes months after the end of season one"; "The Dirty Half Dozen" leads "into the opening scene of Avengers: Age of Ultron" and "Scars" explores its aftermath. MCU Fandom wiki: opens "approximately late May or early June 2014"; "Scars" in May 2015.

Wikipedia (season 3): "set six months after the events that concluded the second season"; "Emancipation" "is set in the aftermath of Civil War". MCU Fandom wiki: first part "December 13, 2015 to January 24, 2016"; "Emancipation" shortly after Civil War's climax (2016).

Wikipedia (season 4): affected by Civil War (2016); Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2 "takes place earlier in the MCU continuity than the season is set". MCU Fandom wiki: the season "ideally picks up in March 2017" (between-season events September 2016).

in_universe.label: 2017–2018 (part in 2091)
in_universe.note: Wikipedia (season 5): "The last four episodes of the season are set during the events of Infinity War, taking place over a single day". MCU Fandom wiki: the team is sent "to the future, in the year 2091"; after returning, an on-screen monitor reads "12-06-2017".

Wikipedia (season 6): "The season begins one year after the end of the fifth season"; Endgame's five-year jump sets it "during a time that half of all life is still dead", and the producers acknowledged "the series no longer lined-up with the films' timeline". MCU Fandom wiki: "space puff incident of 2019"; dated June 2019.

in_universe.label: 2019–2020 (time travel 1931–1983)
in_universe.note: Wikipedia (season 7): categories "Television series set in" 1931, 1955, 1973, 1976, 1982, 1983, 2019, 2020; epilogue "One year later". MCU Fandom wiki: returns to 2019; epilogue "July 4, 2020". Inherits season 6's conflict with Endgame.
